identity.title: Pain out of proportion to examination findings

technique.how: Compare reported pain severity and analgesic requirement with objective findings: for the abdomen, severe continuous pain with a soft, non-tender or minimally tender abdomen; for skin/soft tissue, severe pain or exquisite tenderness extending beyond the visible erythema, or pain disproportionate to a modest cellulitis. Record the discordance explicitly.
technique.prerequisites: Patient able to report pain; opioid or sedative effect accounted for.

interpretation.positive_finding: In a soft-tissue infection, pain out of proportion raised the odds of necrotizing fasciitis about 4.5-fold versus cellulitis in a case-control study; in abdominal pain with vascular risk (AF, atherosclerosis, low flow), it is the classic cue for early mesenteric ischemia and should prompt CT angiography rather than observation.
interpretation.negative_finding: Absence is not reassuring: no single red flag had sufficient sensitivity to rule out necrotizing fasciitis (LR- >=0.5 for all findings), and mesenteric ischemia frequently presents with vague or non-specific pain, especially in the elderly.
interpretation.pitfalls: Late presentations of ischemia develop peritonism, so the sign is transient; analgesia, diabetes, and altered mental status blunt reporting. Distinguishing 'out of proportion' is subjective and undefined in most studies.
interpretation.changes_what: Present: escalate now - CT angiography for suspected mesenteric ischemia; urgent surgical consult for suspected necrotizing infection. Absent: does not lower probability enough to stop work-up.

estimates.target_condition: Necrotizing fasciitis versus cellulitis (case-control): pain-out-of-proportion documented on history/physical examination
estimates.population: All NF cases admitted to a large Canadian tertiary hospital 2004-2013, each matched to two cellulitis controls (retrospective case-control)
estimates.reference_standard: Admitted with diagnosis of necrotizing fasciitis (chart-confirmed) versus cellulitis controls
estimates.quote: The clinical features that most significantly increased the odds of NF were recent surgery (LR+ 7.0) pain-out-of-proportion (LR+ 4.5), diarrhea (LR+ 6.0)

sources.citation: Alayed KA, Tan C, Daneman N. Red Flags for Necrotizing Fasciitis: A Case Control Study. International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases. 2016.

Cudnik MT, Darbha S, Jones J et al. The diagnosis of acute mesenteric ischemia: A systematic review and meta-analysis. Academic emergency medicine : official journal of the Society for Academic Emergency Medicine. 2014.

Fernando SM, Tran A, Cheng W et al. Necrotizing Soft Tissue Infection: Diagnostic Accuracy of Physical Examination, Imaging, and LRINEC Score: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis. Annals of surgery. 2019.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not apply to patients who cannot report pain reliably (sedation, dementia, spinal cord injury); absence of the sign never excludes either diagnosis.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Suspected necrotizing infection or mesenteric ischemia is time-critical: surgical consultation / CT angiography without waiting for laboratory results.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: No interobserver data; 'out of proportion' was extracted from charts retrospectively in Alayed 2016 and is not operationally defined.

extraction_notes: Only one study with a numeric estimate for this specific finding was located: Alayed 2016 (PMID 25975653), a retrospective case-control (NF vs cellulitis); case-control design means no prevalence and LRs may be inflated by spectrum. Its abstract gives LR+ 4.5 but no exact LR- or sensitivity for pain-out-of-proportion, only that 'sensitivity <= 85% and LR- >= 0.5 for all findings' (Abstract, Results); the abstract also reports that absence of all nine red flags gave 'LR- 0.04' (composite, not entered). IJID full text not retrievable via PMC. Mesenteric ischemia: Cudnik 2014 meta-analysis (PMID 24238311) concluded 'Signs, symptoms, and laboratory testing are insufficiently diagnostic for the condition' (Abstract, Conclusions) and pooled no clinical-feature estimates; prevalence in included studies 'ranged from 8% to 60%' (Abstract, Results). No numeric estimate for pain out of proportion in mesenteric ischemia is available. Fernando 2019 (PMID 29672405) NSTI meta-analysis pooled fever, hemorrhagic bullae and hypotension only; pain out of proportion not in abstract and full text not on PMC. Status partially_quantified (one LR direction only, one setting).
